title: Āsār us-Sanādīd
intro: An antiquarian survey of the monuments, inscriptions and scholars of Delhi, and the author's first substantial book. Many of the buildings it records were destroyed in and after 1857, which makes the lithographed plates the substance of the volume rather than its decoration. The English translation, held here as a second edition, runs considerably longer than the Urdu.
sourceFile: 1. Sir Syed Ahmed Khan/Asar us Sanadid in Urdu.pdf

editions.label: English translation — The Remnants of Ancient Heroes
editions.sourceFile: 1. Sir Syed Ahmed Khan/Asar-us-Sanadid - (The Remnants of Ancient Heroes) -- Syed Ahmed Khan.pdf

title: Tārīkh-e-Sarkashī-e-Ẓila Bijnor
intro: A district-level narrative of the events of 1857 in Bijnor, written from the author's own position there as a subordinate judge. It is one of very few contemporaneous accounts of the rebellion written in Urdu by a serving official, and it reads as testimony rather than as history.
sourceFile: 1. Sir Syed Ahmed Khan/Sarkashi Zila Bijnor.pdf

title: Asbāb-e-Baghāwat-e-Hind
intro: The best known of his political writings: an account of the causes of the rebellion, written for circulation among British officials and printed at the author's own expense. It argues that the rising had administrative and religious causes for which the Company's conduct was substantially responsible, and that the absence of Indian representation in the Legislative Council was the root failure.
sourceFile: 1. Sir Syed Ahmed Khan/Causes of the Indian revolt - three essays -- Ahmad Khan, Sayyid.pdf

editions.label: Translation and commentary by his European friends
editions.sourceFile: 1. Sir Syed Ahmed Khan/A Translation of Causes by His European Friends.pdf

title: Khutbāt-e-Aḥmadiyya
intro: A point-by-point answer to William Muir's Life of Mahomet, researched and largely printed in London during the author's visit of 1869 to 1870 and at his own expense. The English edition was issued under the title A Series of Essays on the Life of Mohammed, and is held here as a second edition.
sourceFile: 1. Sir Syed Ahmed Khan/Khutbat Al Ahmadia - Khan, Sir Syed Ahmad.pdf

editions.label: English edition — Life of Muhammad and subjects subsidiary thereto
editions.sourceFile: 1. Sir Syed Ahmed Khan/Life of Muhammad and subjects subsidiary thereto = Khutbat -- Ahmad Khan, Sayyid, Sir.pdf

title: Review on Dr Hunter's Indian Musalmans
intro: A review contesting W. W. Hunter's claim that Indian Muslims were bound by religious obligation to rebel, and disputing his reading of the Wahhabi trials. Short, sharp, and the clearest statement of the author's argument that loyalty and faith were not in conflict.
sourceFile: 1. Sir Syed Ahmed Khan/Sir Syed's Review on Dr. Hunters 'Indian Musalamaan'.pdf

title: A Muhammadan Commentary on the Holy Bible
intro: An unfinished commentary on the Book of Genesis and the Gospels, written to argue that the Muslim scriptures and the Biblical ones could be read as continuous rather than as rivals. It is the most unusual thing he wrote, and it found almost no audience on either side.
sourceFile: 1. Sir Syed Ahmed Khan/A Muhammadan Commentary on the Holy Bible.pdf

title: Āʾīn-e-Akbarī
intro: His edition of Abū'l Faẓl's sixteenth-century administrative gazetteer of the Mughal empire, prepared with his own annotations. The editing of Persian chronicles was the scholarly work that preceded his political writing, and it is the reason the later argument is so heavily documented.
sourceFile: 1. Sir Syed Ahmed Khan/Sir Syeds Ain e Akbari.pdf

title: Safarnāma-e-London
intro: The record of the visit to England of 1869 to 1870 — the journey that produced the Khutbāt, the plan for Tahzīb ul-Akhlāq, and eventually the college at Aligarh. Written largely as letters home, it is candid about money, illness and homesickness in a way none of his public writing is.
sourceFile: 1. Sir Syed Ahmed Khan/Safarnama e London - Sir Syed.pdf

title: Safarnāma-e-Panjāb
intro: An account of a tour of the Punjab undertaken to raise support and funds for the Aligarh college. It is a fundraising diary as much as a travelogue, and it shows the institution being assembled town by town.
sourceFile: 1. Sir Syed Ahmed Khan/Safarnama e Panjab - Sir Syed.pdf

title: Essays on the Advancement of Learning and Education for the Muslims of India
intro: A gathered volume of the essays and addresses on education that make the case Aligarh was built on: that the community's problem was not political disadvantage but the absence of modern instruction, and that the two could not be argued about separately.
sourceFile: 1. Sir Syed Ahmed Khan/Essays - Advancement for Learning & Education for Mooslims of India.pdf

title: Writings and Speeches of Sir Syed Ahmad Khan
intro: A modern compilation edited by Shan Mohammad, gathering the political speeches and public letters into one volume. It is the most convenient single point of entry to his political writing, and — as with any compilation — its selection is itself an argument about what he was.
sourceFile: 1. Sir Syed Ahmed Khan/Writings and Speeches of Sir Syed Ahmad Khan - Compiled by Shan Mohammad.pdf

title: Tafsīr ul-Qurʾān
intro: The unfinished commentary that reads revelation as consistent with natural law, and the work that earned him the polemical label nechari. It attracted more published refutation in his lifetime than anything else he wrote. At over thirteen hundred pages this is the largest single document in the collection.
sourceFile: 1. Sir Syed Ahmed Khan/Religious/Tafseer ul Quraan - Sir Syed.pdf

title: Sīrat-e-Farīdiyya
intro: A life of the Mughal noble and scholar Farīd ud-Dīn, written as family history as much as biography — the author's own ancestry ran through the same Delhi service milieu. An early work, and one of the few places his antiquarian and religious interests meet directly.
sourceFile: 1. Sir Syed Ahmed Khan/Religious/Seerat e Fareedia by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan.pdf

title: Jilā ul-Qulūb bi Zikr il-Maḥbūb
intro: A short devotional treatise on the remembrance of the Prophet, and among the earliest of his surviving writings. Read against the commentary of forty years later, it marks how far the argument travelled.
sourceFile: 1. Sir Syed Ahmed Khan/Religious/Jila ul Quloob Ba Zikr e Mahmood.pdf

title: The Gospel According to Sayyid Ahmad Khan
intro: A study of Sir Syed's religious thought by the Jesuit scholar Christian W. Troll, concentrating on the theology rather than the politics. This is scholarship about him rather than writing by him, and it is catalogued separately for that reason.
sourceFile: 1. Sir Syed Ahmed Khan/The Gospel According to Sayyid Ahmad Khan (1817-1898) Christian Troll.pdf

title: The Spirit of Islam
intro: The most widely read book by any of the eleven: a life of the Prophet and an account of the faith written for a sceptical English readership. It went through many editions and remains in print. Its readiness to argue on the ground of reason rather than authority made it a formative text for a generation of Indian Muslim students.
sourceFile: 2. Ameer Ali/The Spirit Of Islam_ A History Of The Evolution And Ideals -- Ameer Ali.pdf

title: A Short History of the Saracens
intro: A single-volume political history of the Muslim world from the seventh century onward, written to supply what the author regarded as an absent counterweight to European narratives of decline. It is a work of advocacy in the shape of a textbook, and was used as one for decades.
sourceFile: 2. Ameer Ali/A Short History of the Saracens - Ameer Ali.pdf

title: Mohammedan Law
intro: A systematic treatment of Muslim personal law for use in Anglo-Indian courts, and the work that made his professional reputation. It became a standard authority and is still cited in South Asian judgments. At eight hundred and sixty pages it is the longest English volume in the collection.
sourceFile: 2. Ameer Ali/Mohammedan law (Ali, Syed Ameer, 1849-1928).pdf

title: The Ethics of Islam
intro: A lecture arguing that Islamic ethics rest on individual moral responsibility rather than on ritual compliance — the same case as the larger books, compressed to an evening's address.
sourceFile: 2. Ameer Ali/Ethics of Islam - Syed Ameer Ali.pdf

title: The Moslem Festivities
intro: A short descriptive account of the festivals of the Muslim year, written for readers with no prior knowledge of them. Slight beside the treatises, but it shows the register he reached for when explaining rather than arguing.
sourceFile: 2. Ameer Ali/The Moslem Festivities (1892) Syed Ameer Ali.pdf

title: Memoirs and Other Writings
intro: The autobiographical fragment he left, printed with a selection of letters and occasional pieces. The memoir breaks off well before the Privy Council years, so the most consequential part of his life is the part he did not write down.
sourceFile: 2. Ameer Ali/Memoirs-And-Other-Writings-Of-Syed-Ameer-Ali - Digital Library of India.pdf

title: Āyāt-e-Bayyināt
intro: The most substantial book he produced: a theological work written partly in defence of Sir Syed's naturalist reading of the Qur'an and partly to hold the Aligarh position back from its more extreme formulations. It is the clearest statement of what the movement's second generation thought it was defending.
sourceFile: 3. Mohsin ul Mulk/Aayaat E Bayyenat - Nawab Mohsin ul Mulk.pdf

title: Taqlīd aur ʿAmal bil-Ḥadīth
intro: An argument on the limits of following established juristic authority and the conditions under which the ḥadīth may be acted on directly — the central methodological question of the Aligarh reform programme, argued in its own vocabulary rather than in the reformers'.
sourceFile: 3. Mohsin ul Mulk/Taqleed aur Amal bil Hadees.pdf

title: Kitāb ul-Maḥabbat wa'l-Shauq
intro: A treatise on love and longing in the devotional sense, standing somewhat apart from the controversialist writing that occupies the rest of his shelf. Evidence that the Aligarh administrator had a contemplative register he rarely used in public.
sourceFile: 3. Mohsin ul Mulk/Kitabul Mohabbat Wal Shauq - Nawab Mohsin ul Mulk.pdf

title: Makātīb
intro: Collected letters. The correspondence of the man who ran Aligarh after Sir Syed's death is candid about money, factions and the political calculation behind the Simla Deputation in a way none of the public documents are.
sourceFile: 3. Mohsin ul Mulk/Makateeb - Nawab Mohsin ul Mulk.pdf

title: Response to Lepel Griffin on the Indian Muhammadans
intro: A reply to Sir Lepel Griffin's characterisation of Indian Muslims in the British press. It belongs to the same genre as Sir Syed's answer to Hunter — a rebuttal written in English, for English readers, contesting a description before it hardened into policy.
sourceFile: 3. Mohsin ul Mulk/Response to Lepel Griffin on Indian Muhammadans.pdf

title: The First Lecture
intro: An address, printed as a pamphlet, of the kind the Muhammadan Educational Conference existed to circulate. The lecture was the movement's characteristic form: delivered to a few hundred, printed for a few thousand.
sourceFile: 3. Mohsin ul Mulk/The First Lecture - Nawab Mohsin ul Mulk.pdf

title: Kaifiyat-e-Tashrīf Āwarī-e-Sir Habībullāh Khān
titleUrdu: کیفیت تشریف آوری سر حبیب اللہ خاں
intro: A twenty-page account of a visit by Sir Habibullah Khan, printed as an occasional pamphlet. The smallest item on this shelf, and a reminder that much of the Aligarh paper trail consists of exactly this kind of thing.
sourceFile: 3. Mohsin ul Mulk/Kaifiyat Tashreef Aawari Sir Habibullah Khan - Nawab Mohsin ul Mulk.pdf

title: Letters of Viqar ul Mulk and Mohsin ul Mulk
intro: A working correspondence between the two men who ran Aligarh after Sir Syed. It is candid about money, factions and political calculation, and it is the best surviving record in this collection of how the Simla Deputation was actually assembled.
sourceFile: 4. Viqar ul Mulk/Letters of Viqar ul Mulk & Mohsin ul Mulk.pdf

title: Nawāb Viqār ul-Mulk kī Rāʾe: Aligarh Muslim University
titleUrdu: علی گڑھ مسلم یونیورسٹی سے متعلق نواب وقار الملک کی رائے
intro: His stated position on the Muslim university question — the campaign to turn the Aligarh college into a degree-granting university independent of government control, and the issue on which he eventually resigned the trust secretaryship.
sourceFile: 4. Viqar ul Mulk/AIMU se Mutaliq Nawab Viqar ul Mulk ki Raye.pdf

title: Muslim University aur Musalmānoṉ kī Maẕhabī Taʿlīm o Tarbiyat
titleUrdu: مسلم یونیورسٹی اور مسلمانوں کی مذہبی تعلیم و تربیت
intro: Sixteen pages arguing that a Muslim university had to provide religious instruction as well as modern subjects, against the view that it should confine itself to the second. The smallest document in the collection, and the sharpest statement of the disagreement that ran through Aligarh's second generation.
sourceFile: 4. Viqar ul Mulk/Muslim University Aur Musalmanon Ki Mazhabi Taleem-o-tarbiyat - Viqar ul Mulk.pdf

title: India in Transition
intro: A study of Indian constitutional futures written during the First World War, proposing a federated South Asia of largely self-governing provinces within the Empire. Read after 1940 it is a document from a road not taken, and its author lived long enough to see the alternative.
sourceFile: 5. Agha Khan III/India In Transition - Aga Khan III.pdf

title: The Memoirs of Aga Khan: World Enough and Time
intro: Written near the end of a long public life, and the only sustained first-person account by any of the eleven of the negotiations that produced separate electorates, the Round Table Conferences and partition. He was present at all of them, which is a claim none of the others can make.
sourceFile: 5. Agha Khan III/The memoirs of Aga Khan - World Enough and Time - Aga Khan III, 1877-1957.pdf

title: Paighām-e-ʿAmal
intro: Twenty-four pages, and the only item held for him. A call to action in the Khilafat register — the form he worked in, which was the meeting and the pamphlet rather than the book. That this shelf is nearly empty is a fact about how he worked, not a gap in the archive.
sourceFile: 6. Shawkat Ali/Paigham e Amal - by Maulana Shaukat Ali Khan.pdf

title: Selected Writings and Speeches, Volume 1
intro: The first of two volumes gathering the English journalism and the platform speeches. The prose is the reason he is remembered as a writer: fast, ironic, addressed to English readers in their own register and entirely unintimidated by them.
sourceFile: 7. Maulana Muhammad Ali Jawhar/Selected Writings And Speeches Of Mauluna Mohamed Ali, Volume 1.pdf

title: Selected Writings and Speeches, Volume 2
intro: The second volume, running into the Khilafat years and the break with Congress. Read against the first, it tracks a writer moving from argument inside a shared polity to argument about whether one existed.
sourceFile: 7. Maulana Muhammad Ali Jawhar/Selected Writings And Speeches - Volume 2.pdf

title: Speeches of Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar
intro: A short volume of the platform speeches, taken down as delivered. He was among the most effective orators of the period and the transcripts carry the timing, which the edited compilations tend to smooth away.
sourceFile: 7. Maulana Muhammad Ali Jawhar/Speeches of Maulana Muhammad Ali Jawhar.pdf

title: Essays of Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar
intro: Five hundred pages of collected essays and leading articles, the bulk of his surviving prose in one volume. This is where the journalism sits when it is read as a body of work rather than as a run of newspapers.
sourceFile: 7. Maulana Muhammad Ali Jawhar/Essays of Molana Muhammad Ali Jawhar.pdf

title: The Problem of the Hijaz and the Ibn Sauds
intro: On the Saudi conquest of the Hijaz and the question of who should hold custody of the holy cities — the issue that occupied the Khilafat movement after the caliphate itself was abolished, and that split it.
sourceFile: 7. Maulana Muhammad Ali Jawhar/Problem of Hijaz and the Ibn Sauds.pdf

title: Majmūʿa-e-Kalām
intro: His collected verse. He took the pen-name Jauhar and wrote seriously in Urdu throughout, though the poetry has always been read in the shadow of the journalism rather than beside it.
sourceFile: 7. Maulana Muhammad Ali Jawhar/Majmua Kalam of Muhammad Ali Jawhar.pdf

title: Jazbāt-e-Jauhar: Poetry Written in Jail
intro: Verse written during imprisonment. Twenty-six pages, and the most personal document on this shelf — the same voice as the leading articles, with the audience removed.
sourceFile: 7. Maulana Muhammad Ali Jawhar/Poetry whilst in Jail - Jazbaat e Jawhar.pdf

title: Now or Never: Are We to Live or Perish Forever?
intro: Four pages, issued from Cambridge and signed by a handful of students. It is the first appearance in print of the name Pakistan and of the acronym its author built for it. The League's delegates to the Round Table Conference declined to take it up; within a decade it was the name of a national demand.
sourceFile: 8. Ch. Rahmat Ali/Now_or_Never Pamphlet - Chaudhry Rahmat Ali.pdf

title: The Millat of Islam and the Menace of Indianism
intro: A restatement of the 1933 argument in far more absolute terms, rejecting any conception of a shared Indian nationality. Ten pages, and the distance between its tone and that of the first pamphlet is the whole history of the intervening years.
sourceFile: 8. Ch. Rahmat Ali/The Millat of Islam and the Menace of Indianism.pdf

title: Pakistan: The Fatherland of the Pak Nation
intro: The full elaboration of his scheme, complete with maps proposing further Muslim states across the subcontinent. It is the most complete statement of a plan that was, by the time it appeared, already overtaken by the events it had helped to name.
sourceFile: 8. Ch. Rahmat Ali/Pakistan - Chaudhry Rahmat Ali.pdf

title: Complete Works of Rahmat Ali, Volume 1
intro: A collected edition assembled long after his death, gathering the pamphlets with editorial apparatus. Useful as a single point of access, and worth reading as a document of how his reputation was being argued for in the 1970s.
sourceFile: 8. Ch. Rahmat Ali/Complete Works Of Rahmat Ali Vol 1 (1978).pdf

title: Presidential Address, Allahabad
intro: The address to the All-India Muslim League in December 1930 proposing the amalgamation of Punjab, the North-West Frontier Province, Sindh and Baluchistan into a single state. Whether that was a proposal for a separate country or for an autonomous unit within a federated India is still argued over. This volume prints the address in both Urdu and English with the surrounding context, which is the right way to read a disputed text.
sourceFile: 09. Allama Iqbal/Allama-Iqbal-Address-Allahbad-1930-Urdu-English-with-Background.pdf

title: Pakistan: The Heart of Asia
intro: The speeches of the tour of the United States and Canada in May and June 1950: a new country's prime minister explaining it to an audience that had barely heard of it. It is the only document in this collection written from inside the state rather than in argument for it.
sourceFile: 11. Liaquat Ali Khan/Pakistan The Heart of Asia - Speeches in the United States and Canada, May and June, 1950 by the Prime Minister of Pakistan.pdf
